steps.tx: **Raynaud phenomenon** is an episodic, reversible vasospastic disorder affecting digital arteries and arterioles in response to cold exposure or emotional stress. The classic triphasic color sequence begins with intense pallor or **white blanching** from digital ischemia, followed by cyanosis or **blue discoloration** from deoxygenation, and concludes with erythema or **red reperfusion**.
steps.say: Raynaud phenomenon is an episodic digital vasospasm triggered by cold or emotional stress. The classic response exhibits ischemic pallor, cyanosis, and reperfusion erythema.

vis.caption: Classic triphasic digital response: ischemic pallor, cyanosis, and reperfusion erythema. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Distinguishing **primary Raynaud phenomenon** or Raynaud disease from secondary disease is critical. Primary Raynaud begins under **age 30**, exhibits symmetric bilateral episodes, normal nailfold capillaroscopy, **negative ANA serology**, normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and zero tissue necrosis or digital gangrene.
steps.say: Primary Raynaud disease occurs in young individuals with symmetric attacks. Nailfold capillaries, autoantibodies, and inflammatory markers are entirely normal without ulceration.

left.title: Primary Raynaud disease
points: Symmetrical attacks with no digital ulcers

right.title: Secondary Raynaud phenomenon
points: Onset after age 30 or male sex
Enlarged capillary loops and positive autoantibodies

steps.tx: **Secondary Raynaud phenomenon** arises from underlying connective tissue disorders, most notably **systemic sclerosis** in over 90 percent of cases, mixed connective tissue disease, and systemic lupus erythematosus. Red flags include onset **after age 30**, asymmetric distribution, excruciating pain, digital pitting scars, ulcerations, or digital gangrene.
steps.say: Secondary Raynaud phenomenon links to underlying autoimmune disease, especially systemic sclerosis. Warning signs include onset after age 30, digital ulceration, and severe pain.

steps.tx: **Nailfold capillaroscopy** is the most sensitive non-invasive bedside investigation to distinguish primary from secondary Raynaud. In early systemic sclerosis, capillaroscopy shows **giant dilated capillary loops** exceeding 50 micrometres and microhemorrhages, progressing in late disease to severe **capillary drop-out**, extensive avascular areas, and disorganized neoangiogenesis.
steps.say: Nailfold capillaroscopy distinguishes primary from secondary disease. Systemic sclerosis displays giant capillary loops, microhemorrhages, and progressive vascular dropout.

nodes.label: Normal parallel hairpin capillary loops in primary Raynaud
Early SSc pattern: giant dilated loops (>50 micrometres)
Late SSc pattern: extensive capillary dropout and avascular desert

steps.tx: General and non-pharmacologic management constitutes foundational care for all patients. Measures include keeping the entire core body warm with layered thermal clothing, wearing insulated gloves and socks, strict **complete cessation of tobacco smoking**, and strict avoidance of sympathomimetic decongestants, ergot derivatives, and non-selective beta-blockers.
steps.say: Conservative management requires keeping the core body warm and avoiding chilling. Complete tobacco cessation and avoiding sympathomimetic drugs are mandatory.

steps.tx: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are the initial pharmacological treatment of choice. Oral **nifedipine at 30 to 60 mg daily** in extended-release formulation or **amlodipine at 5 to 10 mg daily** relaxes vascular smooth muscle, reducing the frequency, duration, and severity of vasospastic digital attacks.
steps.say: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are first-line pharmacotherapy for Raynaud phenomenon. Extended-release nifedipine reduces attack frequency and severity.

nodes.label: Cold-induced calcium influx in digital vascular smooth muscle
Dihydropyridine blockade with nifedipine 30 to 60 mg daily
Arteriolar vasodilation and decreased digital attack frequency

steps.tx: For patients with inadequate clinical response or intolerable ankle edema from calcium channel blockers, **phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors** are highly effective second-line therapies. Oral **sildenafil at 20 mg three times daily** or **tadalafil at 20 mg alternate days** increases intracellular cyclic GMP, enhancing digital blood flow and healing refractory ulcers.
steps.say: Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors provide effective add-on therapy for refractory vasospasm. Sildenafil elevates cyclic GMP to improve digital perfusion.

right.title: Second-line: PDE-5 inhibitors
points: Effective for active digital ulcer healing

steps.tx: Severe acute digital ischemia, critical digital ulcers, or impending gangrene requires emergency hospital admission and continuous intravenous prostacyclin infusions with **iloprost**. To prevent recurrent digital ischemic ulcers in systemic sclerosis, oral **bosentan**, a dual endothelin receptor antagonist, significantly reduces the formation of new ulcers.
steps.say: Critical digital ischemia requires hospital admission and intravenous iloprost infusions. Oral bosentan prevents recurrent digital ulcers in systemic sclerosis.
